s1.syndrome_frame: Cardiovascular syndrome with arrhythmia, heart failure, and thromboembolic phenomena
salient_findings: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate
Multiple intracardiac thrombi and pulmonary emboli
key_facts: Patient is a 45-year-old African man
Symptoms include palpitations, fatiguability, bipedal edema, weight loss, and diarrhea
10 pack-year smoking history
Vital signs: Blood pressure 136/87 mm Hg, fast atrial fibrillation with ventricular rates of 170 beats/min
Bipedal edema present
Cardiac auscultation: S1 with loud, palpable P2, pansystolic murmurs in tricuspid and mitral areas
Thyroid-stimulating hormone: <0.01 mIU/L, Free T4: 39.2 pmol/L, Thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor antibody: 39.33 IU/L
D-dimer: 5.48 mg/L
Electrocardiogram shows rapid atrial fibrillation, biventricular hypertrophy, and right axis deviation
Echocardiography shows biventricular enlargement, left atrial dilatation, moderate mitral stenosis, severe mitral regurgitation, and severe tricuspid regurgitation
Left ventricular ejection fraction: 39%, Pulmonary artery systolic pressure: 77 mm Hg
Multiple intracardiac thrombi in left atrial appendage, posterior mitral leaflet, right ventricular outflow tract, and proximal pulmonary artery
Bilateral lower-lobe acute pulmonary emboli on CT Pulmonary Angiogram

shortlist.label: Hyperthyroid heart disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has symptoms and lab results consistent with hyperthyroidism, including atrial fibrillation and elevated free T4 levels

shortlist.label: Rheumatic heart disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has mitral stenosis and severe mitral regurgitation, which are common complications of rheumatic heart disease

shortlist.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has biventricular enlargement and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, which are characteristic of dilated cardiomyopathy

shortlist.label: Pulmonary embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has bilateral lower-lobe acute pulmonary emboli on CT Pulmonary Angiogram

shortlist.label: Atrial fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has fast atrial fibrillation with ventricular rates of 170 beats/min, which is a primary diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's low thyroid-stimulating hormone level (<0.01 mIU/L), high free T4 level (39.2 pmol/L), and presence of thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor antibody (39.33 IU/L) indicate hyperthyroidism, which can cause atrial fibrillation, biventricular hypertrophy, and other cardiac symptoms presented in the case

rejected.label: Rheumatic heart disease
rejected.why: No mention of a history of rheumatic fever or valve disease typical of rheumatic heart disease

rejected.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has biventricular enlargement, the primary cause appears to be hyperthyroidism rather than a direct cardiomyopathic process

rejected.label: Pulmonary embolism
rejected.why: Although the patient has pulmonary emboli, they are likely a consequence of the cardiac disease (e.g., atrial fibrillation) rather than the primary diagnosis

rejected.label: Atrial fibrillation
rejected.why: Atrial fibrillation is a symptom rather than a disease entity; the underlying cause, which appears to be hyperthyroidism, is the more appropriate diagnosis
